name: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
description: Persistent inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning.
historyRequirement: At least six months; childhood symptoms before 12; evidence in multiple settings.
reviewLimit: Sleep, anxiety, depression and learning difficulties can resemble attention problems. Toddlers are not a default ADHD case.

name: Autism spectrum disorder
description: Developmental differences in social communication alongside restricted or repetitive patterns.
historyRequirement: Earlier developmental history is essential; recent events cannot create autism.
reviewLimit: Do not infer intellectual disability, lack of empathy or one universal speech style.

name: Specific learning disorder
description: Persistent difficulties in reading, writing or mathematics.
historyRequirement: Difficulties despite targeted assistance for at least six months; educational history.
reviewLimit: Language exposure, teaching opportunity and sensory conditions need consideration; not an IQ guess.

name: Language disorder
description: Developmental difficulties acquiring and using language.
historyRequirement: Developmental and language-assessment history; no synthetic diagnosis from a short transcript.
reviewLimit: NIDCD's developmental language disorder terminology is related, not an automatic DSM equivalence; hearing and multilingual context matter.

name: Intellectual developmental disorder (intellectual disability)
description: Intellectual and adaptive-functioning limitations beginning during development.
historyRequirement: Prior developmental assessment and everyday support needs, not fabricated test scores.
reviewLimit: Do not equate limited speech with low intelligence or use the older adult profile to imply developmental disability.

name: Tourette's disorder (Tourette syndrome)
description: A childhood-onset pattern involving motor and vocal tics.
historyRequirement: Tic history over a year and onset before adulthood; verify exact manual wording.
reviewLimit: Text alone cannot display motor findings; swearing is not a required feature.

name: Major depressive disorder
description: An impairing depressive episode involving low mood or reduced interest, with associated changes.
historyRequirement: A major depressive episode has a two-week duration anchor; evaluate the broader mood history.
reviewLimit: Consider bipolar episodes, medical/substance effects and grief. A sadness slider is insufficient.

name: Persistent depressive disorder
description: A sustained depressive course rather than one brief low-mood episode.
historyRequirement: Adult history generally spans at least two years; child/adolescent rules require manual verification.
reviewLimit: A 90-day log cannot establish a chronic course; distinguish superimposed episodes.

name: Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder (DMDD)
description: Severe recurrent outbursts with persistent irritability between them.
historyRequirement: At least a year; onset before 10; first diagnosis not before 6 or after 18 in APA's rule.
reviewLimit: Differentiate episodic mania and other explanations. Do not automatically combine with ODD; age-summary discrepancy documented.

name: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder
description: A recurring, impairing mood pattern related to the menstrual cycle.
historyRequirement: Document cycle relationship; exact prospective confirmation rules remain to be checked.
reviewLimit: Stage and name alone cannot establish menstruation; distinguish exacerbation of another condition.

name: Bipolar I disorder
description: A history of mania; depressive episodes may also occur.
historyRequirement: Mania usually at least seven days, or shorter when hospitalization is necessary; full episode review required.
reviewLimit: Not ordinary daily mood swings; consider substances, medical causes and psychosis chronology.

name: Bipolar II disorder
description: Hypomanic and major depressive episodes, without a manic episode.
historyRequirement: Author separate past episodes; confirm exact hypomania duration and exclusions against the manual.
reviewLimit: Not simply a milder version of bipolar I; current depression alone does not distinguish it.

name: Cyclothymic disorder
description: A chronic pattern of subthreshold elevated and depressive symptoms.
historyRequirement: Longitudinal course required; exact adult/youth duration rules await full-manual verification.
reviewLimit: Do not produce alternating hourly moods and label them cyclothymia.

name: Generalized anxiety disorder
description: Difficult-to-control worry across areas of life with interference.
historyRequirement: Most days over at least six months; age-specific symptom counts must be verified.
reviewLimit: Ordinary stress, other anxiety presentations, substances and medical conditions.

name: Panic disorder
description: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks with ongoing concern or behavior change.
historyRequirement: At least a month of subsequent worry or change; document recurrent attacks.
reviewLimit: An isolated attack is not panic disorder; medical explanations remain possible.

name: Social anxiety disorder
description: Fear of scrutiny or negative evaluation that restricts participation.
historyRequirement: At least six months with meaningful interference.
reviewLimit: Differentiate ordinary shyness, communication differences and body-image concerns.

name: Specific phobia
description: Focused fear and avoidance around a particular object or situation.
historyRequirement: Persistent course required; exact criteria and duration need manual review.
reviewLimit: Do not pathologize developmentally ordinary fears or actual danger.

name: Agoraphobia
description: Avoidance linked to difficulty escaping or obtaining help in feared situations.
historyRequirement: Document distinct situation types and persistent course; verify full criteria.
reviewLimit: Not synonymous with staying home, and not dependent on having panic disorder.

name: Separation anxiety disorder
description: Developmentally excessive separation fears that interfere with life.
historyRequirement: Age-specific duration and developmental expectations require verification.
reviewLimit: Toddler separation distress can be ordinary development; do not infer a disorder from it.

name: Selective mutism
description: Anxiety-linked inability to speak in certain situations despite speaking elsewhere.
historyRequirement: Document the pattern across people/settings; verify duration and language exclusions.
reviewLimit: Not deliberate defiance; a fluent chatbot alone would misrepresent the presentation.

name: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)
description: Intrusive unwanted thoughts and/or driven rituals that are time-consuming or impairing.
historyRequirement: Document recurring pattern and interference; do not invent a six-month threshold.
reviewLimit: Not mere neatness; unwanted intrusive thoughts are not the person's intentions.

name: Body dysmorphic disorder
description: Distressing appearance preoccupation with repeated checking or comparison.
historyRequirement: Persistent preoccupation, repetitive behavior and impairment must be authored.
reviewLimit: Differentiate eating-related weight/shape concerns; avoid appearance reassurance loops.

name: Hoarding disorder
description: Difficulty discarding possessions leading to compromised living space.
historyRequirement: Longstanding accumulation and functional impact; a week cannot create an established clutter history.
reviewLimit: Differentiate ordinary collecting and cognitive or medical contributors.

name: Trichotillomania (hair-pulling disorder)
description: Recurrent hair pulling with consequences and difficulty stopping.
historyRequirement: Author the course, attempts to stop and impact; exact exclusions need checking.
reviewLimit: Do not make it a moral failure or equate it automatically with suicidal self-injury.

name: Excoriation (skin-picking) disorder
description: Repeated skin picking causing lesions and unsuccessful efforts to stop.
historyRequirement: Pattern and impairment, with medical and other explanations considered.
reviewLimit: Do not generate injury instructions or assume every skin problem is psychiatric.

name: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD)
description: Trauma-linked intrusion, avoidance, arousal and changes in mood/cognition.
historyRequirement: Symptoms longer than one month; qualifying exposure and onset chronology are separate facts.
reviewLimit: Not every stressful event meets the exposure requirement; preschool criteria differ.

name: Acute stress disorder
description: An impairing post-trauma reaction within the early time window.
historyRequirement: Three days to one month after trauma.
reviewLimit: Do not relabel all immediate reactions as PTSD or force later PTSD development.

name: Adjustment disorders
description: Distress or impairment associated with an identifiable stressor.
historyRequirement: Begins within three months; ordinarily ends within six months after the stressor/consequences end.
reviewLimit: Differentiate ordinary adjustment and another disorder better explaining symptoms.

name: Prolonged grief disorder
description: Persistent disabling grief beyond expected cultural context.
historyRequirement: Loss at least 12 months earlier in adults or six months in children/adolescents.
reviewLimit: Grief alone is not illness; introduced as a DSM-5-TR diagnosis, not an original DSM-5 Section II label.

name: Reactive attachment disorder
description: An early-childhood attachment-related presentation associated with severely insufficient care.
historyRequirement: Requires a specific developmental and caregiving history; exact age rules unresolved here.
reviewLimit: Not a synonym for insecure attachment or a conclusion from one caregiver interaction.

name: Disinhibited social engagement disorder
description: An attachment-related pattern of unusually indiscriminate social approach.
historyRequirement: Requires severe insufficient-care history and developmental criteria.
reviewLimit: Not simply being friendly; never invent neglect from personality traits.

name: Depersonalization/derealization disorder
description: Recurring or persistent detachment experiences with reality testing retained.
historyRequirement: Author course and exclusions; no universal synthetic day threshold.
reviewLimit: Distinguish psychosis, substances and neurological explanations.

name: Dissociative amnesia
description: Autobiographical memory gaps beyond ordinary forgetting.
historyRequirement: Specific missing periods and preserved knowledge must be authored.
reviewLimit: Do not fill gaps with invented recovered memories or assumed abuse.

name: Dissociative identity disorder
description: Disruptions in identity and memory requiring careful differential assessment.
historyRequirement: Longitudinal evidence and explicit memory boundaries; not randomly changing personalities.
reviewLimit: Do not conflate with schizophrenia or portray theatrical automatic switching.

name: Somatic symptom disorder
description: Distressing bodily symptoms accompanied by disproportionate symptom-related thoughts or behavior.
historyRequirement: Document persistent concern and impairment; verify precise duration wording.
reviewLimit: Symptoms are real; medical illness can coexist. Normal tests alone are not a diagnosis.

name: Illness anxiety disorder
description: Preoccupation with serious illness when somatic symptoms are absent or limited.
historyRequirement: Longer-term pattern needed; exact threshold not verified here.
reviewLimit: Do not dismiss new symptoms or assume avoidance means lack of concern.

name: Functional neurological symptom disorder (conversion disorder)
description: Involuntary neurological symptoms, such as weakness or movement difficulties, that require a positive clinical assessment.
historyRequirement: Neurological assessment evidence is needed before authoring a confirmed diagnosis.
reviewLimit: This search verified terminology, not a complete criteria/evidence package. Chat cannot replace examination.

name: Anorexia nervosa
description: Restrictive eating with low weight in context and weight/shape-related disturbance.
historyRequirement: Course, growth/weight context and medical assessment must be authored.
reviewLimit: No procedural weight-loss content; appearance alone cannot establish a diagnosis.

name: Bulimia nervosa
description: Binge episodes accompanied by compensatory behavior.
historyRequirement: Document episode frequency and duration; verify full DSM thresholds.
reviewLimit: Differentiate binge-eating disorder and anorexia presentations; medical complications matter.

name: Binge-eating disorder
description: Repeated distressing binge episodes without the regular compensatory pattern of bulimia.
historyRequirement: Verify frequency and duration against the manual before case approval.
reviewLimit: Body size alone is not the diagnosis; avoid moral judgments about eating.

name: Avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID)
description: Restricted intake associated with sensory concerns, low interest or feared consequences, with significant impact.
historyRequirement: Feeding/developmental history and consequences; psychosocial interference may qualify without low weight.
reviewLimit: Distinguish ordinary picky eating and medical causes; not driven by the anorexia-style weight/shape concern.

name: Enuresis
description: Recurrent urinary wetting considered in developmental and medical context.
historyRequirement: Toileting development, frequency and persistence; exact DSM gates need checking.
reviewLimit: Do not assign this diagnosis to ordinary toddler accidents.

name: Encopresis
description: Recurrent fecal soiling requiring developmental and bowel-history assessment.
historyRequirement: Document toileting history, constipation and course; verify full diagnostic gates.
reviewLimit: Avoid blame; a mental-health interview cannot exclude bowel disease.

name: Insomnia disorder
description: Difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep with daytime consequences despite opportunity to sleep.
historyRequirement: Common chronic anchor: at least three nights weekly for at least three months.
reviewLimit: A short sleep diary is not the total disorder duration; consider circadian and breathing problems.

name: Oppositional defiant disorder
description: An impairing pattern of oppositional or irritable behavior requiring contextual assessment.
historyRequirement: Persistent, developmentally unusual pattern; verify duration/frequency and exclusion rules.
reviewLimit: Do not confuse communication difficulty, fear or situational conflict with a disorder.

name: Conduct disorder
description: A persistent serious behavior pattern affecting others' rights or major norms.
historyRequirement: Longitudinal examples and differential assessment; exact gates require manual review.
reviewLimit: Avoid criminality stereotypes, invented offenses or using diagnosis to predict an individual's violence.

name: Alcohol use disorder
description: Impaired control over alcohol use with distress or harmful consequences.
historyRequirement: Symptoms assessed within a 12-month window; this does not require uninterrupted use for a year.
reviewLimit: Quantity alone does not establish the disorder; withdrawal can require medical care.

name: Cannabis use disorder
description: A substance-specific pattern of impaired control and harmful consequences.
historyRequirement: Substance-specific criteria and chronology need verification; distinguish use, intoxication and withdrawal.
reviewLimit: Exposure or medically supervised physiological dependence alone is not enough; avoid invented doses or detox advice.

name: Opioid use disorder
description: A substance-specific pattern of impaired control and harmful consequences.
historyRequirement: Substance-specific criteria and chronology need verification; distinguish use, intoxication and withdrawal.
reviewLimit: Exposure or medically supervised physiological dependence alone is not enough; avoid invented doses or detox advice.

name: Stimulant use disorder
description: A substance-specific pattern of impaired control and harmful consequences.
historyRequirement: Substance-specific criteria and chronology need verification; distinguish use, intoxication and withdrawal.
reviewLimit: Exposure or medically supervised physiological dependence alone is not enough; avoid invented doses or detox advice.

name: Sedative, hypnotic, or anxiolytic use disorder
description: A substance-specific pattern of impaired control and harmful consequences.
historyRequirement: Substance-specific criteria and chronology need verification; distinguish use, intoxication and withdrawal.
reviewLimit: Exposure or medically supervised physiological dependence alone is not enough; avoid invented doses or detox advice.

name: Tobacco use disorder
description: A substance-specific pattern of impaired control and harmful consequences.
historyRequirement: Substance-specific criteria and chronology need verification; distinguish use, intoxication and withdrawal.
reviewLimit: Exposure or medically supervised physiological dependence alone is not enough; avoid invented doses or detox advice.

name: Gambling disorder
description: Repeated gambling with impaired control and consequential harm.
historyRequirement: Past-year pattern, not a single bet or loss.
reviewLimit: Do not provide betting strategies or use financial loss alone as diagnosis.

name: Schizophrenia
description: Psychotic, negative and cognitive features with a characteristic course and impairment.
historyRequirement: Overall disturbance at least six months, with active-phase requirements and exceptions checked separately.
reviewLimit: Not DID and not automatic violence; distinguish reported perceptions from objective world facts.

name: Schizophreniform disorder
description: Schizophrenia-like presentation distinguished partly by shorter duration.
historyRequirement: At least one month and less than six months; follow-up can change the formulation.
reviewLimit: Not a conclusion from one strange statement; longer-term outcome cannot be assumed.

name: Brief psychotic disorder
description: A short episode of unusual perceptions, beliefs or disorganization, followed by return to earlier functioning.
historyRequirement: Exact duration, return-to-baseline and exclusion requirements need dedicated verification.
reviewLimit: Name verified; do not instantiate until the full course is authored.

name: Delusional disorder
description: A separate psychotic disorder requiring careful assessment of belief, context and functioning.
historyRequirement: Exact duration and exclusions require full-manual review.
reviewLimit: Do not classify unfamiliar cultural or religious beliefs as delusions.

name: Schizoaffective disorder
description: A course combining psychotic experiences with substantial mood episodes, including psychosis outside mood episodes.
historyRequirement: Must author relative timing of mood and psychosis; complete rules not verified in this search.
reviewLimit: Not shorthand for any combination of depression and hallucinations.

name: Delirium
description: Acute fluctuating changes in attention and awareness with medical context.
historyRequirement: Hours-to-days change from baseline; fluctuations matter.
reviewLimit: Requires a medical-assessment training scenario, not ordinary stable outpatient role-play.

name: Mild neurocognitive disorder
description: Acquired cognitive decline with everyday independence largely maintained.
historyRequirement: Evidence of decline from prior functioning; testing and etiology context needed.
reviewLimit: Not ordinary ageing or automatically Alzheimer's disease; MCI and DSM labels are not a universal code crosswalk.

name: Major neurocognitive disorder
description: Acquired cognitive decline that interferes with independent daily functioning.
historyRequirement: Author premorbid baseline, course, cause and assessment evidence.
reviewLimit: Older age alone cannot assign dementia; avoid inventing cognitive-test results.

name: Borderline personality disorder
description: A longstanding pattern involving emotion regulation, self-image and relationships.
historyRequirement: Longitudinal pattern, not a brief crisis. Youth cases need separate specialist review.
reviewLimit: Avoid 'manipulative patient' scripts; differentiate episodic bipolar symptoms and trauma-related conditions.

name: Avoidant personality disorder
description: A longstanding pattern of social inhibition and rejection sensitivity with impairment.
historyRequirement: Pervasive pattern across contexts; not inferred from a recent anxious week.
reviewLimit: Compare social anxiety and cultural context; ordinary introversion is not a disorder.

name: Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder
description: A longstanding rigid pattern around order, perfection and control.
historyRequirement: Pervasive developmental history and impairment must be established.
reviewLimit: Distinct from OCD; conscientiousness alone is not psychopathology.

name: Gender dysphoria
description: Clinically significant distress or impairment related to gender incongruence.
historyRequirement: Age/puberty-specific criteria and persistence require appropriate review.
reviewLimit: Transgender or gender-diverse identity itself is not a disorder; no assumptions from pronouns.

name: Complex PTSD — ICD-11 comparison
description: ICD-11 PTSD with additional difficulties in emotion regulation, self-concept and relationships.
classification: ICD-11; not a separate DSM-5-TR diagnosis
historyRequirement: Use a distinct ICD-11 framework; do not mix criteria sets.
reviewLimit: Not a separate DSM-5-TR diagnosis; prolonged trauma alone does not establish it.

name: Gaming disorder — ICD-11 comparison
description: Impaired gaming control with priority over other activities and significant harm.
classification: ICD-11; DSM-5-TR Internet Gaming Disorder is further-study
historyRequirement: Normally a 12-month pattern in WHO's overview; use the full ICD-11 requirements.
reviewLimit: DSM-5-TR Internet Gaming Disorder is a further-study condition, not an equivalent established DSM diagnosis.

name: No disorder assigned
description: A comparator for ordinary variation, stress or insufficient evidence.
classification: Not a disorder; original training-design proposal
historyRequirement: Document only authored experiences; no diagnosis is forced.
reviewLimit: This is a proposed training option, not a DSM disorder.
